vtl #

The V Tensor Library

[![Mentioned in Awesome V][awesomevbadge]][awesomevurl] [![CI][workflowbadge]][workflowurl] [![Docs][docsbadge]][docsurl] [![Full ML][fullmlbadge]][fullmlurl] [![Benchmarks][benchmarksbadge]][benchmarksurl] [![License: MIT][licensebadge]][licenseurl] ![VSL Backed][vslbackedbadge] ![CUDA Optional][cudaoptionalbadge] ![Vulkan f32][vulkanbadge]

VTL is a pure-V tensor library for numerical computing and machine learning — n-dimensional arrays, autograd, linear algebra via VSL, and a full neural network module.

Train small neural networks, experiment with autograd, and use VSL-backed CPU, CUDA, and Vulkan compute paths from one V-native API.

vlang.io | Docs | Tutorials | NumPy/ML migration | Histograms | PyTorch parity | Burn comparison | ML Roadmap | Contributing | VSL

VTL and VSL architecture

View SVG source · PNG 

import vtl
t := vtl.from_array([1.0, 2, 3, 4], [2, 2])!
t.get([1, 1])
// 4.0

Features

  • Tensors — create, slice, indexed take/take_nd/take_flat/put, choose/select, round_decimals, nan_to_num, compress, indices, pad, set membership, reshape, transpose, move/roll axes, N-D diagonal views, NumPy-style Kronecker products, broadcast, map/reduce, einsum, and complex128 storage with elementwise and matrix products
  • Autograd — reverse-mode AD; arbitrary computational graphs
  • Neural networks — Sequential API; Linear, Conv2D, LSTM, Attention, …
  • Losses & optimizers — MSE, MAE, BCE, Hinge, Focal, CrossEntropy, Huber; Adam, AdamW, NAdam, RAdam, SGD, …
  • Linear algebra — VSL-backed real matmul and general eigensolvers, pure-V complex128 matmul, solve, QR, LU, Cholesky, SVD, pinv
  • Hardware — zero-copy Tensor.data for C libs; optional CUDA and Vulkan training paths

ML Release Highlights

The ML beta scope is the high-level VTL API: tensors, autograd, layers, losses, optimizers, datasets, and CPU training. CUDA and Vulkan paths are available for opt-in validation and early adopters, but remain experimental backend accelerators rather than stable user contracts.

Area Status
f32 training Sequential + MSE + Adam smoke tests
CUDA Experimental opt-in Linear/Conv2D forward; f64 Linear/Conv2D/Dropout backward; activation chain and Adam slots
Vulkan Experimental opt-in f32 Linear, Conv2D same-padding, ReLU/Sigmoid/Softplus/SELU/HardSwish, fused Adam shader
Datasets MNIST, IMDB, CIFAR-10 loaders plus CI-safe synthetic examples
Benchmarks VTL vs NumPy/PyTorch scripts and PR benchmark workflow

For memory-safe local commands, see DEV_LIGHTWEIGHT.md.

Quick start

import vtl
import vtl.autograd
import vtl.nn.layers
import vtl.nn.models
import vtl.nn.optimizers

mut ctx := autograd.ctx[f32]()
mut model := models.sequential_from_ctx[f32](ctx)
model.input([784])
model.linear(256)
model.linear(10)
model.mse_loss()

input_tensor := vtl.zeros[f32]([64, 784])
mut x := ctx.variable(input_tensor)
y_pred := model.forward(x)!

target := vtl.zeros[f32]([64, 10])
mut loss_val := model.loss(y_pred, target)!
loss_val.backprop()!

mut opt := optimizers.adam_optimizer[f32](optimizers.AdamOptimizerConfig{
    learning_rate: 0.001
})
opt.build_params(model.info.layers)
opt.update()!

Installation

VTL uses VSL for linear algebra. The core vtl module works without optional system BLAS/LAPACK, but LA features need VSL.

Follow VSL install instructions, then:

v install vtl

Testing

# Run the full scoped suite from ~/.vmodules; compiler parallelism is disabled
# to keep the local memory ceiling predictable.
cd ~/.vmodules
systemd-run --user --scope --property=MemoryMax=4G --property=MemorySwapMax=0 \
    env VJOBS=2 VTL_NO_PARALLEL=1 ./vtl/bin/test

See DEV_LIGHTWEIGHT.md for memory-safe subsets in CI. See PAIRED_RELEASES.md for VTL/VSL candidate release validation.

Contributors

VTL's early development was inspired by vnum, part of the Vlang Num group, and the work of Christopher Zimmerman. The core was reimplemented while keeping that lineage and inspiration. The original vnum work carried a BSD 3-Clause license with attribution to vlang-num contributors; the historical license text is preserved in the VTL repository history. This acknowledgment records that history and does not change VTL's current license, shown below.

fn abs #

fn abs(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[f64]

abs is the NumPy-style alias for absolute.

fn absolute #

fn absolute(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[f64]

absolute returns the magnitude of every complex element as a float64 tensor. math.hypot scales its inputs to avoid unnecessary overflow and underflow.

fn acos_promoted #

fn acos_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

acos_promoted computes elementwise inverse cosine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn acosh_promoted #

fn acosh_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

acosh_promoted computes elementwise inverse hyperbolic cosine using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn add_promoted #

fn add_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], b &Tensor[U]) !&Tensor[R]

add_promoted adds real numeric or boolean tensors after converting both operands to the explicitly selected NumPy-style result dtype. The output type R must match the operation's NumPy result dtype.

fn add_scalar_left_promoted #

fn add_scalar_left_promoted[R, T, U](scalar U, a &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

add_scalar_left_promoted adds a tensor to a weak numeric or complex scalar using NumPy-style promotion.

fn add_scalar_promoted #

fn add_scalar_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], scalar U) !&Tensor[R]

add_scalar_promoted adds a weak numeric or complex scalar using NumPy-style promotion. R must be the inferred result dtype; this explicit type is required by V's statically typed generic return values.

fn advanced_index #

fn advanced_index[T](t &Tensor[T], indices []&Tensor[int]) !&Tensor[T]

advanced_index selects values using one integer coordinate tensor per input axis. Coordinate tensors are broadcast together, and each output element is read from the matching coordinate tuple. The result is an independent row-major copy. This API handles full coordinate tuples; mixing coordinate tensors with slices or scalar indices is not supported here.

fn arange #

fn arange[T](start f64, stop f64, step f64, params TensorData) !&Tensor[T]

arange returns evenly spaced values in the half-open interval [start, stop). The direction of step determines whether the result is ascending or descending.

arccos applies the principal inverse complex cosine to every element.

fn arccosh(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

arccosh applies the principal inverse complex hyperbolic cosine to every element.

fn argpartition #

fn argpartition[T](t &Tensor[T], kth int) !&Tensor[int]

argpartition returns local indices that place kth at its sorted position along the last axis. The order of the other indices is unspecified.

fn argpartition_axis #

fn argpartition_axis[T](t &Tensor[T], kths []int, axis int) !&Tensor[int]

argpartition_axis partially orders local indices along axis. The returned tensor has the same shape as t and supports multiple kth positions.

fn argsort #

fn argsort[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[int]

argsort returns stable ascending sort indices along the last axis.

fn argsort_axis #

fn argsort_axis[T](t &Tensor[T], axis int) !&Tensor[int]

argsort_axis returns the stable ascending sort indices along axis. Returned indices are local to that axis; floating-point NaNs sort to the end.

fn argwhere #

fn argwhere[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[int]

argwhere returns the coordinates of non-zero elements as a row-major tensor with shape [number of matches, input rank].

fn array_index #

fn array_index(indices &Tensor[int]) TensorIndex

array_index selects positions using an integer coordinate tensor. All coordinate tensors in a mixed_index call are broadcast together.

fn asin_promoted #

fn asin_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

asin_promoted computes elementwise inverse sine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn asinh_promoted #

fn asinh_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

fn atan2_promoted #

fn atan2_promoted[R, T, U](y &Tensor[T], x &Tensor[U]) !&Tensor[R]

atan2_promoted computes elementwise atan2 for real numeric or boolean tensors. It returns float64 when either input is float64 or a >=32-bit integer; other results use float32. NumPy float16 results for booleans and <=8-bit integers are widened because VTL does not support float16.

fn atan_promoted #

fn atan_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

atan_promoted computes elementwise inverse tangent values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn atanh_promoted #

fn atanh_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

atanh_promoted computes elementwise inverse hyperbolic tangent using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

binary_promoted_auto selects the NumPy-style result dtype at runtime. The returned sum type preserves the concrete tensor dtype for callers that need statically typed values; use promoted_tensor_dtype or match on the result.

fn binomial #

fn boolean_index #

fn boolean_index[T](t &Tensor[T], mask &Tensor[bool]) !&Tensor[T]

boolean_index selects values where mask is true. The mask shape must match the leading tensor dimensions; any remaining tensor dimensions are retained after the selected-element axis. The result is an independent row-major copy, matching NumPy's a[mask] behavior.

fn choose #

fn choose[T](indices &Tensor[int], choices []&Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

choose selects values from choices using integer indices. Choices broadcast to one common shape, and indices broadcast to that shape. Each index must be in the range [0, choices.len).

fn clip_tensor #

fn clip_tensor[T](t &Tensor[T], lower &Tensor[T], upper &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

clip_tensor clamps values using broadcastable lower and upper bounds. It computes the result in one pass so callers do not need separate maximum and minimum tensors or intermediate results. Stride-based offsets avoid creating per-element coordinate arrays, including when an input is a view.

fn column_stack #

fn column_stack[T](ts []&Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

column_stack stacks 1-D arrays as columns into a 2-D array.

fn complex_angle #

fn complex_angle(input &Tensor[complex.Complex], degrees bool) !&Tensor[f64]

complex_angle returns the phase of each value in radians, or degrees when requested. The result range follows atan2 and is [-pi, pi].

fn complex_is_finite #

fn complex_is_finite(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[bool]

complex_is_finite reports whether both components of each value are finite.

fn complex_is_inf #

fn complex_is_inf(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[bool]

complex_is_inf reports whether either component of each value is infinite.

fn complex_is_nan #

fn complex_is_nan(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[bool]

complex_is_nan reports whether either component of each value is NaN.

fn compress #

fn compress[T](condition &Tensor[bool], t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

compress selects flattened values at positions where condition is true. As in NumPy, a condition shorter than the input stops selection at its length; extra condition values are ignored.

fn compress_axis #

fn compress_axis[T](condition &Tensor[bool], t &Tensor[T], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

compress_axis selects slices along axis using a one-dimensional condition. If condition is shorter than the axis, the remaining slices are omitted.

fn concatenate #

fn concatenate[T](ts []&Tensor[T], data AxisData) !&Tensor[T]

concatenate concatenates two Tensors together

fn conj #

fn conj(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

conj returns the complex conjugate of every element in a complex tensor.

fn copysign[T](magnitude &Tensor[T], sign &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

copysign returns the magnitude of magnitude with the sign bit of sign. Both f32 and f64 inputs broadcast to a common output shape.

fn copysign_promoted #

fn copysign_promoted[R, T, U](magnitude &Tensor[T], sign &Tensor[U]) !&Tensor[R]

copysign_promoted applies the sign bit of a real numeric or boolean tensor to another tensor's magnitude, with NumPy-style float output promotion.

fn cos(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

cos applies the complex cosine to every element.

fn cos_promoted #

fn cos_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

cos_promoted computes elementwise cosine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn cosh #

fn cosh(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

cosh applies the complex hyperbolic cosine to every element.

fn cosh_promoted #

fn cosh_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

cosh_promoted computes elementwise hyperbolic cosine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn count_nonzero #

@[direct_array_access]
fn count_nonzero[T](t &Tensor[T]) int

count_nonzero counts non-zero values across every tensor dimension.

fn count_nonzero_axes #

fn count_nonzero_axes[T](t &Tensor[T], axes []int, keepdims bool) !&Tensor[int]

count_nonzero_axes counts non-zero values along multiple axes. Negative axes are supported, axes must be unique, and an empty axis list preserves the input shape while converting each value to zero or one.

fn count_nonzero_axis #

fn count_nonzero_axis[T](t &Tensor[T], axis int, keepdims bool) !&Tensor[int]

count_nonzero_axis counts non-zero values along one axis. By default the reduced axis is removed; set keepdims to retain it with length one.

fn degrees_promoted #

fn degrees_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

degrees_promoted converts radians to degrees with NumPy-style float output promotion.

fn diagonal #

fn diagonal[T](input &Tensor[T], params DiagonalData) !&Tensor[T]

diagonal returns a view along the diagonal of two axes of an N-D tensor. The selected axes are removed and the diagonal axis is appended to the result, following NumPy's shape convention. The view shares input storage. VTL tensors remain mutable, so writes through the result update the input.

fn diagonal_readonly #

fn diagonal_readonly[T](input &Tensor[T], params DiagonalData) !&ReadOnlyDiagonalView[T]

diagonal_readonly returns a storage-sharing diagonal view with a read-only API. The legacy diagonal function remains writable for compatibility.

fn diff #

fn diff[T](t &Tensor[T], n int, axis int) !&Tensor[T]

diff computes the n-th discrete difference along an axis. Negative axes count from the end, and n=0 returns a row-major copy of the input.

fn digitize #

fn digitize[T](values &Tensor[T], bins &Tensor[T], right bool) !&Tensor[int]

digitize assigns values to monotonic bins. Increasing and decreasing edge arrays are supported; right selects which interval owns an edge value.

fn dirichlet #

fn dirichlet[T](alpha &Tensor[T], sample_shape []int, params TensorData) !&Tensor[f64]

dirichlet returns normalized Gamma samples. The final output axis contains categories and sample_shape defines the preceding axes.

fn divide_promoted #

fn divide_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], b &Tensor[U]) !&Tensor[R]

divide_promoted performs NumPy-style true division for numeric tensors and booleans. Complex inputs produce complex128; real inputs produce float32 only when the promoted input dtype is float32, and float64 otherwise.

fn divide_scalar_left_promoted #

fn divide_scalar_left_promoted[R, T, U](scalar U, a &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

divide_scalar_left_promoted performs NumPy-style true division with a weak scalar as the numerator.

fn divide_scalar_promoted #

fn divide_scalar_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], scalar U) !&Tensor[R]

divide_scalar_promoted performs true division by a weak numeric scalar using NumPy-style promotion. R must be the inferred result dtype.

fn dstack #

fn dstack[T](ts []&Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

dstack stacks arrays in sequence depth wise (along third axis)

fn dtype_of #

fn dtype_of[T]() DType

dtype_of returns the VTL dtype corresponding to the compile-time type T.

fn einsum #

fn einsum[T](subscripts string, operands ...&Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

einsum evaluates an Einstein summation expression over one or more tensors. It supports alphabetic axis labels, explicit or implicit output labels, repeated labels for diagonals, broadcasting of size-one axes, and any number of operands. Ellipses expand to the leading axes and are right-aligned across operands, enabling batched expressions such as ...ij,...jk->...ik.

When the output is omitted, labels that occur exactly once are returned in alphabetical order, following NumPy's implicit-output convention.

fn ellipsis_index #

fn ellipsis_index() TensorIndex

ellipsis_index expands to enough full axes to cover the unindexed dimensions. At most one ellipsis is allowed in a mixed_index call.

empty exposes this operation as part of the public API.

fn pow_promoted #

fn pow_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], b &Tensor[U]) !&Tensor[R]

pow_promoted computes elementwise powers after broadcasting. Numeric pairs use promote_types(dtype_ofT, dtype_ofU); boolean pairs return int8, matching NumPy. Integer powers keep exact-width wrapping arithmetic and reject negative integer exponents. Complex pairs use the principal branch; 64-bit integers cannot be combined with a floating output because conversion could lose integer precision.

fn promote_types #

fn promote_types(a DType, b DType) !DType

promote_types returns the common dtype for two array dtypes. Its numeric rules are modeled on NumPy, using the integer and floating-point types VTL currently supports. If VTL has no signed integer width that can represent both inputs, it promotes to float64. Mixing strings with other dtypes is rejected; scalar-value weak promotion is not part of this dtype-only API.

fn promoted_tensor_dtype(t PromotedTensor) DType

promoted_tensor_dtype returns the runtime-selected dtype of a promoted tensor.

radians_promoted converts degrees to radians with NumPy-style float output promotion.

	options MultiIndexOptions) !&Tensor[int]

ravel_multi_index converts one integer coordinate tensor per dimension to flat indices. Coordinate tensors broadcast together. The result shape is their broadcast shape. mode applies raise, wrap, or clip bounds handling to every axis; axis_modes may instead specify one mode per axis. Order selects C (row-major) or F (column-major) flattening.

remainder_promoted returns the element-wise NumPy remainder of real numeric tensors after dtype promotion and broadcasting. Complex inputs are rejected. Integer zero divisors produce zero; floating-point zero divisors produce NaN.

rot90_k rotates in the first two dimensions by k counterclockwise quarter-turns.

fn scalar_left_promoted_auto[T, U](scalar U, a &Tensor[T], operation PromotedArithmetic) !PromotedTensor

scalar_left_promoted_auto selects the NumPy-style result dtype for a weak scalar on the left, preserving noncommutative operation order.

fn scalar_promoted_auto #

fn scalar_promoted_auto[T, U](a &Tensor[T], scalar U, operation PromotedArithmetic) !PromotedTensor

scalar_promoted_auto selects the NumPy-style result dtype for a weak scalar on the right, without requiring the caller to provide the output type.

fn searchsorted #

fn searchsorted[T](sorted &Tensor[T], values &Tensor[T], side SearchSide) !&Tensor[int]

searchsorted returns insertion positions for values in an ascending 1-D tensor. The input is assumed to be sorted; each query uses binary search.

fn searchsorted_descending #

fn searchsorted_descending[T](sorted &Tensor[T], values &Tensor[T], side SearchSide) !&Tensor[int]

searchsorted_descending returns insertion positions for values in a descending 1-D tensor. The input is assumed to be sorted; each query uses binary search. The output has the same shape as values.

fn select #

fn select[T](conditions []&Tensor[bool], choices []&Tensor[T], default T) !&Tensor[T]

select picks the value from the first choice whose condition is true at each output position. Conditions and choices broadcast to a common shape; default is used where no condition is true.

@[inline]

seq exposes this operation as part of the public API.

fn sin #

sin applies the complex sine to every element.

fn sin_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

sin_promoted computes elementwise sine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn sinh #

fn sinh(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

sinh applies the complex hyperbolic sine to every element.

fn sinh_promoted #

fn sinh_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

sinh_promoted computes elementwise hyperbolic sine values using the same output dtype rules as sqrt_promoted.

fn slice_all #

fn slice_all(step int) !TensorIndex

slice_all selects the whole axis, optionally traversing it in reverse.

fn slice_from #

fn slice_from(start int, step int) !TensorIndex

slice_from selects from start through the end of the axis in step increments. A negative step traverses toward the beginning.

fn slice_index #

fn slice_index(start int, stop int, step int) !TensorIndex

slice_index selects an explicit Python-style [start:stop:step] range. Negative boundaries count from the end; a zero step is rejected.

fn slice_to #

fn slice_to(stop int, step int) !TensorIndex

slice_to selects from the beginning of the axis through stop in step increments.

fn sort #

fn sort[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

sort returns a copy sorted along the last axis, matching NumPy's default.

fn sort_axis #

fn sort_axis[T](t &Tensor[T], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

sort_axis returns a copy sorted in ascending order along axis. Floating-point NaNs sort after all non-NaN values, and equal values keep their input order.

fn sqrt #

fn sqrt(input &Tensor[complex.Complex]) !&Tensor[complex.Complex]

sqrt applies the principal complex square root to every element.

fn sqrt_promoted #

fn sqrt_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

sqrt_promoted computes elementwise square roots for real numeric or boolean tensors. It returns float64 for float64 and >=32-bit integer inputs, and float32 otherwise; NumPy float16 results are widened because VTL does not support float16.

fn stack #

fn stack[T](ts []&Tensor[T], data AxisData) !&Tensor[T]

stack join a sequence of arrays along a new axis.

fn subtract_scalar_promoted[R, T, U](a &Tensor[T], scalar U) !&Tensor[R]

fn tile #

fn tile[T](t &Tensor[T], reps []int) !&Tensor[T]

tile repeats t as a block according to reps. Repetition dimensions align from the right; shorter reps are padded with ones on the left, as in NumPy.

fn triangular #

fn triangular(left f64, mode f64, right f64, shape []int, params TensorData) !&Tensor[f64]

triangular returns samples from a triangular distribution using VTL's global stream.

fn tril #

fn tril[T](input &Tensor[T], options TriangularOptions) !&Tensor[T]

tril returns a copy with entries above the k-th diagonal of each trailing matrix set to zero. Inputs must have at least two dimensions.

fn triu #

fn triu[T](input &Tensor[T], options TriangularOptions) !&Tensor[T]

triu returns a copy with entries below the k-th diagonal of each trailing matrix set to zero. Inputs must have at least two dimensions.

fn trunc_promoted #

fn trunc_promoted[R, T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[R]

trunc_promoted truncates elementwise toward zero while preserving the input dtype.

fn ufunc_accumulate #

fn ufunc_accumulate[T](input &Tensor[T], identity T, operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

ufunc_accumulate returns the inclusive prefix operation in logical row-major order, preserving the input shape.

fn ufunc_accumulate_axis #

fn ufunc_accumulate_axis[T](input &Tensor[T], axis int, identity T, operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

fn ufunc_at #

fn ufunc_at[T](mut target &Tensor[T], indices []int, updates []T, operation fn (T, T) T) !

ufunc_at mutates flat logical positions in sequence. Repeated indices are applied repeatedly, and updates may contain one broadcast value or one value per index. Bounds are validated before the first mutation.

fn ufunc_binary #

fn ufunc_binary[T](left &Tensor[T], right &Tensor[T], operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

fn ufunc_binary_into #

fn ufunc_binary_into[T](left &Tensor[T], right &Tensor[T], output &Tensor[T], where_mask &Tensor[bool], has_where bool, operation fn (T, T) T) !

fn ufunc_outer #

fn ufunc_outer[T](left &Tensor[T], right &Tensor[T], operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

ufunc_outer computes operation(left[i], right[j]) for every flattened logical pair and returns a matrix of shape [left.size, right.size].

fn ufunc_reduce #

fn ufunc_reduce[T](input &Tensor[T], identity T, operation fn (T, T) T) T

ufunc_reduce applies a binary operation in logical row-major order. The identity is returned unchanged for empty inputs.

fn ufunc_reduce_axis #

fn ufunc_reduce_axis[T](input &Tensor[T], axis int, identity T, operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

fn ufunc_reduceat #

fn ufunc_reduceat[T](input &Tensor[T], indices []int, operation fn (T, T) T) !&Tensor[T]

ufunc_reduceat applies a segmented reduction in flattened logical order. Each start must be in bounds; non-increasing adjacent starts select one element, following NumPy's reduceat segment rule.

fn ufunc_unary #

fn ufunc_unary[T](input &Tensor[T], operation fn (T) T) !&Tensor[T]

fn ufunc_unary_into #

fn ufunc_unary_into[T](input &Tensor[T], output &Tensor[T], where_mask &Tensor[bool], has_where bool, operation fn (T) T) !

ufunc_unary_into preserves masked-out values in the caller-owned output.

fn unique #

fn unique[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

unique returns the sorted unique values in a flattened copy of the tensor. Floating-point NaNs are treated as one value and sort after other values.

fn unique_axis #

fn unique_axis[T](t &Tensor[T], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

unique_axis returns lexicographically sorted unique slices along axis.

fn unique_axis_result #

fn unique_axis_result[T](t &Tensor[T], axis int) !UniqueAxisResult[T]

unique_axis_result returns unique slices, occurrence counts, first source axis positions, and inverse indices aligned to the input axis.

fn unique_counts #

fn unique_counts[T](t &Tensor[T]) !UniqueCounts[T]

unique_counts returns sorted unique values and the number of occurrences of each value in the flattened input tensor.

fn unique_first_indices #

fn unique_first_indices[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[int]

unique_first_indices returns the first flattened input index for each sorted unique value.

fn unique_inverse #

fn unique_inverse[T](t &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[int]

unique_inverse returns the unique-value index for each flattened input element. Apply it to unique(t) to reconstruct the input values.

fn unravel_index #

@[direct_array_access]
fn unravel_index(indices &Tensor[int], dimensions []int, options UnravelIndexOptions) ![]&Tensor[int]

unravel_index converts flat indices into one coordinate tensor per axis. Each returned tensor has the same shape as indices. Order selects C (row-major) or F (column-major) decoding.

fn vander #

@[direct_array_access]
fn vander[T](input &Tensor[T], params VandermondeData) !&Tensor[T]

vander returns a Vandermonde matrix built from a one-dimensional input. The default column count is input.size; powers descend by default and increase when requested, matching NumPy's vander convention. T must be a numeric element type.

fn vmap #

fn vmap[T](f fn (&Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T], input &Tensor[T], in_dim int, out_dim int) !&Tensor[T]

vmap applies a tensor function independently over one input axis and stacks the results along the requested output axis. The mapped axis is removed before calling f, so f operates on one sample at a time.

fn vonmises #

fn vonmises(location f64, concentration f64, shape []int, params TensorData) !&Tensor[f64]

vonmises returns angles in [-pi, pi) from VTL's global random stream.

fn vstack #

vstack stack arrays in sequence vertically (row wise)

fn wald #

wald returns samples from a Wald (inverse Gaussian) distribution using VTL's global stream.

fn weibull #

weibull returns samples from the unit-scale Weibull distribution using VTL's global random stream.

interface AnyTensor #

interface AnyTensor[T] {
	shape   []int
	strides []int
	cpu() &Tensor[T]
	vcl() !&Tensor[T]
	str() string
	rank() int
	size() int
	is_matrix() bool
	is_square_matrix() bool

	is_row_major() bool
	is_col_major() bool
	is_row_major_contiguous() bool
	is_col_major_contiguous() bool

mut:
	memory MemoryFormat
}

AnyTensor is an interface that allows for any tensor to be used in the vtl library

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) sum_along_axis[T](axis int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[T]

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) min_along_axes[T](axes []int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[T]

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) max_along_axis[T](axis int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[T]

fn (MaskedArray[T]) max_along_axes #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) max_along_axes[T](axes []int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[T]

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) variance_along_axis[T](axis int, ddof int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

fn (MaskedArray[T]) variance_along_axes #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) variance_along_axes[T](axes []int, ddof int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

variance_along_axes computes population or sample variance over several axes. Empty axes compute elementwise zero variance for valid values.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) std_along_axis #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) std_along_axis[T](axis int, ddof int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) std_along_axes[T](axes []int, ddof int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

std_along_axes computes standard deviation over several axes.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) mean_along_axis #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) mean_along_axis[T](axis int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

mean_along_axis computes the mean of unmasked values per axis slice. Slices with no unmasked values carry a masked NaN result.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) mean_along_axes #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) mean_along_axes[T](axes []int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

mean_along_axes computes means over several axes. Negative axes are supported; duplicate axes are rejected. An empty axes list converts each unmasked value to f64 and preserves the mask.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average[T, W](weights &Tensor[W]) !MaskedValue[f64]

weighted_average computes a weighted mean over valid values. Weights must broadcast to the values shape; masked observations do not contribute either their value or their weight. An entirely masked array returns masked NaN.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average_along_axis #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average_along_axis[T, W](weights &Tensor[W], axis int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

weighted_average_along_axis computes weighted means per slice. Weights may broadcast to the values shape or be a vector matching the selected axis.

fn (MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average_along_axes #

fn (array &MaskedArray[T]) weighted_average_along_axes[T, W](weights &Tensor[W], axes []int, keepdims bool) !MaskedArray[f64]

weighted_average_along_axes reduces several dimensions. Weights must broadcast to the values shape; empty slices are masked and zero-sum valid weights return an error.

fn (Tensor[T]) put #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) put[T](indices &Tensor[int], values &Tensor[T]) !

put replaces values at row-major logical flat indices. Values repeat when there are fewer values than indices. Negative indices count from the end. Invalid indices return an error without changing the tensor.

fn (Tensor[T]) putmask #

@[direct_array_access]
fn (mut t Tensor[T]) putmask[T](mask &Tensor[bool], values &Tensor[T]) !

putmask replaces values where mask is true, in row-major logical order. Update values repeat cyclically by row-major flat position, matching NumPy's putmask semantics. The mask must match the tensor shape exactly.

fn (Tensor[T]) put_with_mode #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) put_with_mode[T](indices &Tensor[int], values &Tensor[T], mode PutMode) !

put_with_mode replaces values at row-major logical flat indices, using mode to handle indices outside the flattened tensor's range. Repeated indices follow row-major write order, so the last value wins. All indices are validated before any writes are made.

fn (Tensor[T]) put_along_axis #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) put_along_axis[T](indices &Tensor[int], values &Tensor[T], axis int) !

put_along_axis writes values at indices along axis. Indices and values must have the same rank as the target and values must match the index shape. The index dimensions outside axis may be smaller than the target dimensions. Negative indices count from the end. When an index is repeated, the last value in row-major iteration order wins. Out-of-range indices return an error before any target values are changed.

fn (Tensor[T]) scatter_add #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) scatter_add[T](indices &Tensor[int], values &Tensor[T], axis int) !

scatter_add adds values at indices along axis. Duplicate indices accumulate in row-major iteration order; negative indices count from the end. An out-of-range index returns an error before any target values are changed.

fn (Tensor[T]) all_axis #

fn (Tensor[T]) any_axis #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) any_axis[T](axis int, keepdims bool) !&Tensor[bool]

any_axis reduces one axis with logical OR. The reduced dimension is removed unless keepdims is true. Empty reductions follow NumPy's identity: false.

fn (Tensor[T]) all_axes #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) all_axes[T](axes []int, keepdims bool) !&Tensor[bool]

all_axes reduces multiple axes with logical AND. Axes may be negative and must be unique. An empty axes list converts values to bool without reducing.

fn (Tensor[T]) any_axes #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) any_axes[T](axes []int, keepdims bool) !&Tensor[bool]

any_axes reduces multiple axes with logical OR. Axes may be negative and must be unique. An empty axes list converts values to bool without reducing.

fn (Tensor[T]) is_finite #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) is_finite[T]() &Tensor[bool]

is_finite returns true where x is not positive infinity, negative infinity, or NaN; false otherwise.

fn (Tensor[T]) is_inf #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) is_inf[T](sign int) &Tensor[bool]

is_inf reports whether t is an infinity, according to sign. If sign > 0, is_inf reports whether t is positive infinity. If sign < 0, is_inf reports whether t is negative infinity. If sign == 0, is_inf reports whether t is either infinity.

fn (Tensor[T]) is_nan #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) is_nan[T]() &Tensor[bool]

is_nan returns true for NaN values and false for finite values and infinities.

fn (Tensor[T]) is_real #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) is_real[T]() &Tensor[bool]

is_real returns true for values with no imaginary component. For complex values, the imaginary component must compare equal to zero.

fn (Tensor[T]) is_complex #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) is_complex[T]() &Tensor[bool]

is_complex returns true for complex values with a nonzero imaginary component. NaN imaginary components are considered complex.

fn (Tensor[T]) array_equal #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) array_equal[T](other &Tensor[T]) bool

array_equal returns true if input arrays have the same shape and all elements compare exactly equal. Floating-point NaNs compare unequal; use isclose for approximate comparisons.

fn (Tensor[T]) array_equiv #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) array_equiv[T](other &Tensor[T]) bool

array_equiv returns true if input arrays are shape consistent and all elements equal. Shape consistent means they are either the same shape, or one input array can be broadcasted to create the same shape as the other one.

fn (Tensor[T]) axis_iterator #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) axis_iterator[T](axis int) &TensorAxisIterator[T]

axis_iterator returns an iterator over the axis of a Tensor, commonly used for reduction operations along an axis.

fn (Tensor[T]) axis_with_dims_iterator #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) axis_with_dims_iterator[T](axis int) &TensorAxisIterator[T]

axis returns an iterator over the axis of a Tensor, commonly used for reduction operations along an axis. This iterator keeps the axis dimension as size 1 instead of removing it

fn (Tensor[T]) take #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take[T](indices []int, axis int) !&Tensor[T]

take returns a copy of the tensor with the values at indices selected along axis. Negative axes and negative indices count from the end. The indices are a one-dimensional list; use slice for range-based views.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_with_mode #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_with_mode[T](indices []int, axis int, mode TakeMode) !&Tensor[T]

take_with_mode selects values along axis, handling out-of-range indices with the requested mode. In .clip mode, negative values clip to zero, matching NumPy's take behavior.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_nd #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_nd[T](indices &Tensor[int], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

take_nd gathers values along one axis using an index tensor. The index tensor's dimensions replace the selected axis in the output shape.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_nd_with_mode #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_nd_with_mode[T](indices &Tensor[int], axis int, mode TakeMode) !&Tensor[T]

take_nd_with_mode gathers with an index tensor and applies mode to every index. The index tensor's dimensions replace the selected axis.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_flat #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_flat[T](indices &Tensor[int]) !&Tensor[T]

take_flat gathers from the row-major logical flattening of a tensor and preserves the shape of the index tensor.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_flat_with_mode #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_flat_with_mode[T](indices &Tensor[int], mode TakeMode) !&Tensor[T]

take_flat_with_mode gathers from row-major logical order and applies mode to indices outside the flattened tensor's range.

fn (Tensor[T]) take_along_axis #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) take_along_axis[T](indices &Tensor[int], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

take_along_axis gathers values using an index tensor with the same rank as the receiver. Non-axis dimensions broadcast; the result's axis length is taken from the index tensor. Negative indices count from the end.

fn (Tensor[T]) get #

@[inline]
fn (t &Tensor[T]) get[T](index []int) T

get exposes this operation as part of the public API.

fn (Tensor[T]) get_checked #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) get_checked[T](index []int) !T

get_checked returns a scalar value at index, or an error if the index rank or any coordinate is outside the tensor bounds. Negative coordinates count from the end of their axis.

fn (Tensor[T]) get_nth #

@[inline]
fn (t &Tensor[T]) get_nth[T](n int) T

get_nth exposes this operation as part of the public API.

fn (Tensor[T]) nth_index #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) nth_index[T](n int) []int

nth_index returns the nth index of a Tensor's shape for n == 2 and a shape of [2, 2] the nth index is [1, 0] and for a shape of [2, 3] and n == 3 the nth index is [0, 1, 1] in sorted order.

fn (Tensor[T]) flip #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) flip[T](axes ...int) !&Tensor[T]

flip returns a copy of t with the selected axes reversed. With no axes, all axes are reversed, matching NumPy's flip default. Negative axes are accepted.

fn (Tensor[T]) masked_select #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) masked_select[T](mask &Tensor[bool]) !&Tensor[T]

masked_select returns the values whose corresponding mask entries are true. The mask must be broadcastable to the tensor shape; values are returned in row-major logical order, including for non-contiguous views.

fn (Tensor[T]) masked_fill #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) masked_fill[T](mask &Tensor[bool], value T) !&Tensor[T]

masked_fill returns a tensor with mask-selected values replaced by value. The mask must be broadcastable to the tensor shape.

fn (Tensor[T]) masked_scatter #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) masked_scatter[T](mask &Tensor[bool], source &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

masked_scatter copies source values, in row-major order, into the true positions selected by a broadcastable mask. The source must contain at least as many values as the mask selects; extra source values are ignored.

fn (Tensor[T]) diag #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) diag[T]() !&Tensor[T]

diag constructs a diagonal array. input must be one dimensional and will be placed along the resulting diagonal

fn (Tensor[T]) diag_flat #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) diag_flat[T]() !&Tensor[T]

diag_flat constructs a diagonal array. the flattened input is placed along the diagonal of the resulting matrix

fn (Tensor[T]) tril #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) tril[T]() &Tensor[T]

tril computes the lower triangle of an array. returns a copy of an array with elements above the diagonal zeroed

fn (Tensor[T]) tril_offset #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) tril_offset[T](offset int) &Tensor[T]

tril_inplace computes the lower triangle of an array. returns a copy of an array with elements above the kth diagonal zeroed

fn (Tensor[T]) tril_inplace #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) tril_inplace[T]() &Tensor[T]

tril_inplace computes the lower triangle of an array. modifies an array inplace with elements above the diagonal zeroed.

fn (Tensor[T]) tril_inpl_offset #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) tril_inpl_offset[T](offset int) &Tensor[T]

tril_inpl_offset computes the lower triangle of an array. modifies an array inplace with elements above the k-th diagonal zeroed.

fn (Tensor[T]) triu #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) triu[T]() &Tensor[T]

triu computes the Upper triangle of an array. returns a copy of an array with elements below the diagonal zeroed

fn (Tensor[T]) triu_offset #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) triu_offset[T](offset int) &Tensor[T]

triu_offset computes the upper triangle of an array. returns a copy of an array with elements below the kth diagonal zeroed

fn (Tensor[T]) triu_inplace #

fn (mut t Tensor[T]) triu_inplace[T]() &Tensor[T]

triu_inplace computes the upper triangle of an array. modifies an array inplace with elements below the diagonal zeroed.

fn (Tensor[T]) nan_to_num #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) nan_to_num[T](params NanToNumConfig) &Tensor[T]

nan_to_num replaces NaN and positive or negative infinity in floating-point tensors. Complex values are handled component-wise; other types are copied.

fn (Tensor[T]) sign #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) sign[T]() &Tensor[T]

sign returns the elementwise sign of each value: -1, 0, or 1. Floating-point NaNs remain NaN. Complex values return their normalized phase, matching NumPy 2.0 and later.

fn (Tensor[T]) heaviside #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) heaviside[T](x1 T) &Tensor[T]

heaviside returns 0 for negative values, 1 for positive values, and x1 for zero values. Floating-point NaNs remain NaN.

fn (Tensor[T]) clip #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) clip[T](min_value T, max_value T) !&Tensor[T]

clip limits tensor values to the inclusive scalar interval [min_value, max_value]. The tensor element type is preserved; NaN values remain NaN.

fn (Tensor[T]) array_split_expl #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) array_split_expl[T](ind []int, axis int) ![]&Tensor[T]

array_split_expl splits an array into multiple sub-arrays. Please refer to the split documentation. The only difference between these functions is that array_split allows indices_or_sections to be an integer that does not equally divide the axis. For an array of length l that should be split into n sections, it returns l % n sub-arrays of size l//n + 1 and the rest of size l//n.

fn (Tensor[T]) split #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) split[T](ind int, axis int) ![]&Tensor[T]

split splits an array into multiple sub-arrays. The array will be divided into N equal arrays along axis. If such a split is not possible, panic

fn (Tensor[T]) split_expl #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) split_expl[T](ind []int, axis int) ![]&Tensor[T]

split_expl splits an array into multiple sub-arrays. The array will be divided into The entries of ind indicate where along axis the array is split. For example, [2, 3] would, for axis=0, result in: ary[:2] ary[2:3] ary[3:]

fn (Tensor[T]) hsplit #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) hsplit[T](ind int) ![]&Tensor[T]

hsplit splits an array into multiple sub-arrays horizontally (column-wise). Please refer to the split documentation. hsplit is equivalent to split with axis=1, the array is always split along the second axis regardless of the array dimension.

fn (Tensor[T]) hsplit_expl #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) hsplit_expl[T](ind []int) ![]&Tensor[T]

hsplit_expl splits an array into multiple sub-arrays horizontally (column-wise) Please refer to the split documentation. hsplit is equivalent to split with axis=1, the array is always split along the second axis regardless of the array dimension.

fn (Tensor[T]) vsplit #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) vsplit[T](ind int) ![]&Tensor[T]

vsplit splits an array into multiple sub-arrays vertically (row-wise). Please refer to the split documentation. vsplit is equivalent to split with axis=0 (default), the array is always split along the first axis regardless of the array dimension.

fn (Tensor[T]) vsplit_expl #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) vsplit_expl[T](ind []int) ![]&Tensor[T]

vsplit_expl splits an array into multiple sub-arrays vertically (row-wise). Please refer to the split documentation. vsplit is equivalent to split with axis=0 (default), the array is always split along the first axis regardless of the array dimension.

fn (Tensor[T]) dsplit #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) dsplit[T](ind int) ![]&Tensor[T]

dsplit splits array into multiple sub-arrays along the 3rd axis (depth). Please refer to the split documentation. dsplit is equivalent to split with axis=2, the array is always split along the third axis provided the array dimension is greater than or equal to 3.

fn (Tensor[T]) dsplit_expl #

fn (t &Tensor[T]) dsplit_expl[T](ind []int) ![]&Tensor[T]

dsplit_expl splits array into multiple sub-arrays along the 3rd axis (depth). Please refer to the split documentation. dsplit is equivalent to split with axis=2, the array is always split along the third axis provided the array dimension is greater than or equal to 3.

free releases the generator's underlying pseudorandom engine.

snapshot captures the generator's exact raw PRNG state for replay.

restore replaces this generator's raw PRNG state with a validated snapshot.

uniform returns f64 values in the [minimum, maximum) range.

integers returns seeded int samples from [low, high).

integers_with_endpoint returns seeded int samples from [low, high) or [low, high] when endpoint is true.

fn (RandomGenerator) multivariate_normal #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) multivariate_normal(mean &Tensor[f64], covariance &Tensor[f64], sample_shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

multivariate_normal draws samples with the requested mean and covariance. sample_shape describes the leading sample dimensions; the final output axis contains the variables. Positive-semidefinite covariance matrices are supported, including singular matrices.

fn (RandomGenerator) lognormal #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) lognormal(mean f64, sigma f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

lognormal returns samples whose natural logarithm follows a normal distribution with the given mean and standard deviation.

bernoulli returns bool values sampled with the given probability of true.

fn (RandomGenerator) binomial #

binomial returns the number of successful trials in each sample using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) negative_binomial #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) negative_binomial(n f64, probability f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

negative_binomial counts failures before n successes using this generator's independent stream. n is the positive real-valued success threshold and p is the success probability for each trial.

fn (RandomGenerator) hypergeometric #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) hypergeometric(ngood int, nbad int, nsample int, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

hypergeometric samples the number of good items in draws made without replacement from a population containing ngood good and nbad bad items.

fn (RandomGenerator) multivariate_hypergeometric #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) multivariate_hypergeometric(colors &Tensor[int], nsample int, sample_shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

multivariate_hypergeometric samples category counts without replacement. The final output axis has one count per entry in colors.

fn (RandomGenerator) multinomial #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) multinomial(trials int, probabilities &Tensor[f64], sample_shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

multinomial returns category counts for repeated samples from one categorical distribution. The final output axis contains the categories.

fn (RandomGenerator) exponential #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) exponential(lambda f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

exponential returns f64 samples from an exponential distribution with the given positive finite rate using this generator's independent stream.

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) gumbel(location f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

gumbel returns samples from a Gumbel distribution with the given location and non-negative scale using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) laplace #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) laplace(location f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

laplace returns samples from a Laplace distribution with the given location and non-negative scale using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) cauchy #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) cauchy(location f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

cauchy returns samples from a Cauchy distribution with the given location and positive scale using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) wald #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) wald(mean f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

wald returns samples from a Wald (inverse Gaussian) distribution with the given positive mean and positive scale using this generator's stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) logistic #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) logistic(location f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

logistic returns samples from a Logistic distribution with the given location and non-negative scale using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) pareto #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) pareto(shape_parameter f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

pareto returns samples from the standard Pareto distribution (minimum zero) with the given positive shape parameter and this generator's stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) power #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) power(shape_parameter f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

power returns samples from NumPy's power distribution on [0, 1] using the given positive shape parameter and this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) rayleigh #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) rayleigh(scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

rayleigh returns samples from a Rayleigh distribution with non-negative scale and this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) vonmises #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) vonmises(location f64, concentration f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

vonmises returns angles in [-pi, pi) from a circular distribution with the given location and non-negative concentration using this generator's stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) triangular #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) triangular(left f64, mode f64, right f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

triangular returns samples from a triangular distribution defined by its left endpoint, mode, right endpoint, and this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) geometric #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) geometric(probability f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

geometric returns the number of Bernoulli trials needed for the first success, independently sampled from this generator. Results start at 1.

fn (RandomGenerator) zipf #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) zipf(exponent f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

zipf samples positive integers from a Zipf distribution on this generator's independent stream. The exponent must be finite and greater than one.

fn (RandomGenerator) logseries #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) logseries(probability f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

logseries samples positive integers from a logarithmic-series distribution.

fn (RandomGenerator) poisson #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) poisson(lambda f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[int]

poisson returns integer event counts with the given finite, non-negative expected rate using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) weibull #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) weibull(shape_parameter f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

weibull returns samples from the unit-scale Weibull distribution. The positive shape parameter controls the distribution's tail and hazard rate.

fn (RandomGenerator) chi_square #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) chi_square(degrees_of_freedom f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

chi_square returns samples from a chi-square distribution with the given positive degrees of freedom.

fn (RandomGenerator) noncentral_chi_square #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) noncentral_chi_square(degrees_of_freedom f64, noncentrality f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

noncentral_chi_square returns samples from a noncentral chi-square distribution using this generator's independent stream.

fn (RandomGenerator) student_t #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) student_t(degrees_of_freedom f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

student_t returns samples from the standard Student's t distribution.

fn (RandomGenerator) f_distribution #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) f_distribution(numerator_df f64, denominator_df f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

f_distribution returns samples from an F distribution with the specified numerator and denominator degrees of freedom.

fn (RandomGenerator) noncentral_f #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) noncentral_f(numerator_df f64, denominator_df f64, noncentrality f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

noncentral_f returns samples from a noncentral F distribution.

fn (RandomGenerator) choice #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) choice[T](population &Tensor[T], size int, replace bool) !&Tensor[T]

choice samples values from a tensor's flattened logical order. Without replacement, selected positions are unique; the same value may still occur more than once in the population.

fn (RandomGenerator) choice_weighted #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) choice_weighted[T](population &Tensor[T], weights &Tensor[f64], size int, replace bool) !&Tensor[T]

choice_weighted samples values from a tensor's flattened logical order in proportion to non-negative weights. Without replacement, each selected position is removed from the remaining weight distribution.

fn (RandomGenerator) choice_axis #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) choice_axis[T](population &Tensor[T], size int, axis int, replace bool) !&Tensor[T]

choice_axis samples complete slices along axis and replaces that axis by size.

fn (RandomGenerator) choice_weighted_axis #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) choice_weighted_axis[T](population &Tensor[T], weights &Tensor[f64], size int, axis int, replace bool) !&Tensor[T]

choice_weighted_axis samples complete slices in proportion to non-negative axis weights and replaces that axis by size.

fn (RandomGenerator) permutation #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) permutation(size int) !&Tensor[int]

permutation returns the integers in [0, size) in a seeded random order.

fn (RandomGenerator) permutation_tensor #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) permutation_tensor[T](input &Tensor[T]) !&Tensor[T]

permutation_tensor returns a copy with rows shuffled along the first axis, matching NumPy's permutation behavior for an N-dimensional array.

fn (RandomGenerator) permutation_axis #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) permutation_axis[T](input &Tensor[T], axis int) !&Tensor[T]

permutation_axis returns a copy with slices shuffled along the selected axis. Negative axes are accepted, matching Tensor.take and NumPy's axis convention.

fn (RandomGenerator) gamma #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) gamma(alpha f64, scale f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

gamma returns samples from a Gamma distribution using this generator's independent stream. alpha is the shape and scale is the scale parameter.

fn (RandomGenerator) beta #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) beta(alpha f64, beta f64, shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

beta returns samples from a Beta distribution using this generator's independent stream. alpha and beta are the two positive shape parameters.

fn (RandomGenerator) dirichlet #

fn (mut generator RandomGenerator) dirichlet[T](alpha &Tensor[T], sample_shape []int) !&Tensor[f64]

dirichlet returns samples from a Dirichlet distribution. The final output axes match the concentration tensor's shape; sample_shape is prepended.
